data: My family taught me to leave enough fish for the next season. With 100 tons in the lake, we can catch 50 tons between us and leave 50 to double back to 100. I propose 10 tons each this month—that’s $10,000 apiece, and we can keep earning that every month if we stick together. I’ll commit to 10 tons. Shall we all agree, then review the catches together afterward? John, what do you think?

I’m in for 10 tons, Luke. My family’s livelihood has depended on this lake, and I want our village to keep benefiting from it. Let’s agree not to increase our catches without talking first, and check the revealed totals together each month. John, can you commit to 10 tons too?

Count me in for 10 tons. Keeping this lake healthy means steady work for our families and fish for the village. If anyone catches more than agreed, let’s discuss it rather than start a race to empty the lake. John, are you on board?

I’m on board for 10 tons. My family taught me that a good catch should never come at the expense of the next one. Let’s check the catches together each month and keep our combined take at 50 tons while the lake is full. Jack, will you join us at 10 tons?

I’ll join you at 10 tons. That gives us a clear agreement from all five: 50 tons total, leaving enough to refill the lake next month. Let’s compare the revealed catches afterward and adjust together if the stock changes. I want this lake supporting our village for years to come.

Then we have an agreement: 10 tons each this month. I’ll stick to my share, and we’ll meet again when the catches are revealed. Thanks, everyone—this is how we keep the lake providing for our families.
